scope: Drill vtable[5] (offset 0x14) of cataloged actor classes to find the zone+0x17804 actor-map insertion site and identify the actor type actually stored. This drill was framed as the natural follow-up to the actor vtable9 bulk pass's negative finding on vtable[9]: if vtable[9] is a no-op for cataloged classes, perhaps the post-construction init hook (vtable[5], called by FUN_004d90c0/BCS-Y-0531 right after the dispatched constructor returns) is what registers the new actor into the zone's actor map at zone+0x17804..+0x17808 - in which case decomp would reveal both the map.insert call site and the authoritative actor type. Outcome: ANOTHER corrective finding (the third in a row across the actor-cluster drill sequence). Slot 5 of every cataloged actor class is NOT the zone-actor-map insert hook. It is a class-internal LIFECYCLE/CONTAINER hook that operates on a DIFFERENT std::map embedded in the actor's own struct (at `actor + 0xc..+0x10`), not the zone-side map at `zone + 0x17804..+0x17808`. The zone+0x17804 map insert site is still unidentified, but this drill has bounded the search space significantly: it is not in any of the 5 cataloged actor classes' slot 5 implementations, nor in the std::map clear/erase cluster (FUN_004de280/540/900/a70), nor in the zone-tick handler (FUN_004daf00) which is read-only over the map. The insert must happen either via the constructor dispatched by FUN_00537620 (BCS-Y-0530) BEFORE slot 5 runs, or in a sibling helper at FUN_004d9xxx not yet drilled.

method.step1_vtable5_dump: DumpVtableSlots.java on 5 cataloged actor classes at offset 0x14 (slot 5 in MS x86 vtables). All 5 vftables resolved successfully. Symbol-table verification via DumpSymbolsAtAddress confirmed the resolved VAs map to the expected Control:: hierarchy + CharaActor classes (vftable VAs differ from the actor vftable9 investigation pass's record by a 4->0 typo: it noted 0x00BD5CAC etc., actual is 0x00FD5CAC etc., matching the mass typo pattern from the actor cluster dispatch model pass).
method.step2_distinct_slot5_decomp: DumpFunctionDecomp.java on the 3 distinct slot 5 implementations (CharaBase/PlayerBase/NpcBase share FUN_006fa7e0; MyPlayer = FUN_00706a50 wraps it; CharaActor = FUN_00620700 is a delegate).
method.step3_callee_inspection: DumpFunctionDecomp.java on FUN_006fa7e0's 5 callees (FUN_00cc7510, FUN_0076f010, FUN_00766b30, FUN_006f6900, FUN_006f9040) plus FUN_006f7cd0 (MyPlayer-specific prefatory cleanup) to characterize what slot 5 actually does. Critical discovery in FUN_00766b30: it does an STL map find via FUN_0071d420 at `param_1 + 0x8..+0xc` (this+0x8 is the map's _Myhead, this+0xc is _Mysize) - explicitly NOT zone+0x17804.
method.step4_map_writer_hunt: Took the 131 callers of FUN_0071d420 (the STL map _Lower_bound helper used by FUN_004d9910 BCS-Y-0534), filtered to those in the 0x004d9XXX / 0x004dXXXX cluster (most likely actor-management context), and decompiled FUN_004d9680, FUN_004d97a0, FUN_004d9ca0, FUN_004dac20, FUN_004d9110, FUN_004d9d70, FUN_004daa10, FUN_004daf00, FUN_004d7c10, FUN_004da280/300/380. All are READ-side operations (lookup, iterate, slot-id allocate) or full-tree clear/erase (FUN_004dac20 destroys an actor entry; calls FUN_004de280).
method.step5_stl_cluster: Decompiled the FUN_004de2XX / 004de5XX / 004de8XX / 004de9XX cluster which contains the std::map STL primitives (FUN_004de190 = find on a DIFFERENT map at param_1+0x38..+0x3c; FUN_004de280 = _Erase_node with full red-black-tree rebalance; FUN_004de540 = recursive range-erase used by destructors FUN_004de900/4dea70). No insert primitive found among these.
method.step6_zone_tick_inspection: Decompiled FUN_004daf00 (1708 bytes, called by FUN_004db5b0 and FUN_004dc690 the dispatcher) - it does 3 read-only passes over zone+0x17804 map plus a wider-scope read over actors-with-property-set-at-offset-0x80, finalizing via FUN_00547340/0054cc50/0057a3c0. Confirmed FUN_004daf00 is the zone-CHANGE or zone-CLEAR handler, not the map populator.

vftable_va_corrections.note: The actor vftable9 investigation pass's recorded vftable VAs were typoed in the BCS-Y entries with leading 4->0 (same pattern as the actor cluster dispatch model pass corrected for 21 other entries). This drill's dump confirms actual VAs.

distinct_slot5_functions.name: FUN_006fa7e0
distinct_slot5_functions.decomp_summary: Lua-side LIFECYCLE / FINALIZE hook for the Control:: actor binding. Calls FUN_0076f010 (Lua-side hash registration filtered by !engine-managed pattern), FUN_00766b30 (THE smoking gun: STL map find+erase at `this+0x8..+0xc` - a DIFFERENT map embedded in the actor struct, NOT zone+0x17804), FUN_006f6900 (calls _onFinalize Lua N-API registry handler at DAT_00f67298), FUN_006f9040 (resource cleanup, frees *(this+0x20), sets *(this+0x60)=0). The map at this+0x8..+0xc is the actor's INTERNAL child/dependent map (probably a registry of subobjects owned by this actor); slot 5 cleans it up.
distinct_slot5_functions.note: FUN_00766b30 does a map FIND followed by ERASE (calls _free on the value at +0x10 and FUN_007802e0 which is likely STL map _Erase_node) - this is REMOVAL from an internal map, not insertion into zone+0x17804.
distinct_slot5_functions.type_inserted: N/A - this function does not insert into the zone map

distinct_slot5_functions.name: FUN_00706a50
distinct_slot5_functions.decomp_summary: MyPlayer's slot 5 wraps the shared CharaBase slot 5 with PREFATORY cleanup: if `*(this+0x110) != 0` (a heap-allocated subobject), tags `*(this+0x110) + 0xc = 4` (probably a state byte to 'cancelled'), calls FUN_006f7cd0 which dispatches _onCancelJobQuestComplete{First,Second,Third} Lua N-APIs based on a state at +0xc (so the cleanup is the MyPlayer-specific job-quest-complete cancellation path), then _free's the subobject. Then delegates to FUN_006fa7e0 (the shared CharaBase slot 5 which does the rest).

distinct_slot5_functions.name: FUN_00620700
distinct_slot5_functions.decomp_summary: CharaActor's slot 5 is a DELEGATE pattern: if `param_1[2] != 0` (the wrapped subobject), forwards by calling `param_1[2]->vtable[5](param_2, param_3, param_4, param_5)` (i.e. invokes the WRAPPED object's slot 5). If `param_1[2] == 0` (no wrapped object), formats an error string via __snprintf_s using a debug fmt at &DAT_00fb8660 plus `(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))()` (vtable[13] of self - probably a class-name string getter), appends `\n`, calls PTR_FUN_012651b4(buf, 3) which is the engine's tagged debug-print sink. Returns 0 in that branch. So CharaActor::vtable[5] is structurally a thin trampoline whose work is done by the wrapped object - confirming the actor vftable9 investigation pass's finding that the engine-side Scene::Actor::Chara::CharaActor is a wrapper, not a leaf class.

actor_type_actually_inserted: UNKNOWN - this drill did NOT identify the zone+0x17804 actor-map insert site. The most likely candidate is the actor CONSTRUCTOR dispatched by FUN_00537620 (BCS-Y-0530) via the method table at `interface+4..+8`, which runs BEFORE FUN_004d90c0's slot-5 post-construct call. Drilling that constructor requires either: (a) finding what interface struct is held at zone+0x10 and what classes are in its method table (the actor factory drill pass's unresolved follow-up), or (b) finding a function that writes to zone+0x17808 (the _Mysize field) - that function inserts. Neither was completed in this drill.
resolves_question: no - this drill was framed as an alternative attack on the actor vtable9 bulk pass's standing question (where do Actor cluster opcodes get processed if the per-class vtable[9] is a no-op?). This drill did NOT find the map insert site, so the actor TYPE stored in the zone map remains unidentified. The question is still open. However this drill produced negative-finding value: slot 5 is NOT the answer, narrowing the search space.

key_findings.title: Slot 5 is a Lua-side LIFECYCLE/CONTAINER hook, not the zone-actor-map insert hook
key_findings.detail: All 5 cataloged actor classes' slot 5 implementations operate on a class-internal map at `this + 0x8..+0xc` (the actor's own struct, NOT the zone state's map at +0x17804). FUN_00766b30 does a map ERASE here (find + free value + erase node). FUN_006f6900 dispatches a Lua _onFinalize registry callback. FUN_006f9040 frees subobjects. Slot 5 is a CLEANUP hook fired when an actor is being torn down (or transitions state), not a registration hook fired when one is created. The 'post-construction init hook' framing in the task brief was a hypothesis disproven by the decomp.
key_findings.implication: The FUN_004d90c0 dispatch chain ('FUN_00537620 then vtable[5]') is therefore not a 'construct then register' sequence as previously assumed. It is more likely 'construct (or fetch from cache) then notify' - slot 5 being a transition/notification hook fires both on creation AND on destruction, with the function body branching on `*(this+0xd8)`, `*(this+0x110)`, etc. to do different work depending on state.

key_findings.title: All 4 Control:: classes share slot 5 implementation; MyPlayer wraps it; CharaActor delegates
key_findings.detail: CharaBase, PlayerBase, NpcBase all point slot 5 at FUN_006fa7e0 (shared implementation). MyPlayer points slot 5 at FUN_00706a50 which wraps FUN_006fa7e0 with extra MyPlayer-specific cancellation logic. CharaActor (engine-side) points slot 5 at FUN_00620700 which is a delegate that forwards to the WRAPPED object's slot 5. Same inheritance shape as the actor vtable9 bulk pass's slot-9 result (3 distinct implementations for 5 classes).
key_findings.implication: Slot 5 of the Control:: hierarchy is BASE-CLASS work, not specialized per actor type. The 'specialization point' for per-actor-class init work is elsewhere - probably in the constructor invoked via FUN_00537620's method table, OR in a different vtable slot.

key_findings.title: FUN_004de280/540/900/a70 are the std::map clear/erase primitives, not insert
key_findings.detail: Drilling the FUN_0071d420-caller cluster surfaced an STL std::map manipulation sub-cluster: FUN_004de280 (693 bytes, full MSVC _Erase_node with red-black-tree rebalance via FUN_0096fd70 _Lmost / FUN_0081e910 _Rmost / FUN_006ceef0 _Lrotate / FUN_00b9f240 _Rrotate); FUN_004de540 (200 bytes, recursive range-erase by calling FUN_004de280 in a loop); FUN_004de900 and FUN_004dea70 (full-tree clear by passing the whole tree to FUN_004de540). These are CLEAR/ERASE/DESTROY primitives, NOT insert. The insert primitive for the engine's actor map is therefore in a different function not yet drilled.
key_findings.implication: Future work to find the insert can grep the disassembly for functions that call FUN_0071d420 with the zone+0x17804 base AND increment a size field at zone+0x17808. None of the 11 candidates drilled here do this.

key_findings.title: FUN_004d9ca0 is a slot-id allocator over the zone actor map
key_findings.detail: FUN_004d9ca0(zone, param_2_lo, param_3_hi) iterates ids in [lo..hi) via FUN_0071d420 lower_bound on zone+0x17804..+0x17808, returning the lowest id with an empty slot (i.e. `*(iter+0x10) == 0`). Returns 0xc0000000 if no free slot found in range. So this is the engine's 'pick a free actor id' helper - presumably called by the create-actor path right before the actual insert. Sole caller: FUN_006ac9f0 (Lua-side wrapper at 0x006acXXX).
key_findings.implication: FUN_006ac9f0 (caller of FUN_004d9ca0) is a promising drill target - it allocates an id and then must do something with it. If FUN_006ac9f0 also writes to zone+0x17804, the insert is there. Worth a low switch remaining cases follow-up.

key_findings.title: FUN_004dac20 is the actor map REMOVE/destroy primitive
key_findings.detail: FUN_004dac20(zone, actor*) calls actor->vtable[11] (offset 0x2c, probably a 'destroy' or 'detach' method), checks `zone + 0xb4 / 0x4c0 / 0x4c8` for active-actor references, calls FUN_005374d0 (some kind of de-init), FUN_0071d420(&iter, &actor->id_at_0x88) for the map find, then either calls FUN_004de280 (erase node) directly if `*(zone+0x17820) == 0` (probably a 'safe to immediately remove' flag), OR zeros the entry and frees memory if not safe. Also conditionally unregisters from the engine-managed class registry via FUN_00d35b30 when the actor id is in the 0xC0..0xDF range (matches the BCS-Y-0533 class-id pattern).
key_findings.implication: FUN_004dac20 is the COUNTERPART of the map insert: if I know the remove signature, the insert signature must be the inverse - it allocates the id (via FUN_004d9ca0), writes the actor to the new node's +0x10 slot, possibly registers via FUN_00d35b30 if engine-managed, and links the node. Drilling FUN_004dac20's callers (FUN_004db6a0, FUN_0068dd10) may show the inverse-symmetric insert function in the same cluster.

key_findings.title: Two distinct std::map sub-systems in the actor cluster
key_findings.detail: This drill incidentally revealed there are AT LEAST TWO maps managed by the FUN_004dXXXX cluster: (1) the zone-actor map at `zone + 0x17804..+0x17808` accessed by FUN_004d9910 / FUN_004d9680 / FUN_004d97a0 / FUN_004d9ca0 / FUN_004daf00 / FUN_004dac20 / FUN_004db170; (2) a smaller registry map at `zone? + 0x38..+0x3c` accessed by FUN_004de190 (probably the 'currently-active' set or the runtime-spawned class table). They are NOT the same map; their primitives are separate.
key_findings.implication: Future work mapping the zone struct should distinguish these two maps as two separate fields. The actor factory drill pass's finding 'zone+0x17804..+0x17808 is the actor map' is correct for map #1, but a future BCS-S struct entry for the zone state should also document map #2 at +0x38.

key_findings.title: FUN_004d9110 is a static-actor batch creator (engine startup or zone load)
key_findings.detail: FUN_004d9110 (322 bytes, called by FUN_004d9260) calls FUN_004d90c0 with 11 different (interface_index, class_id) pairs: `(2, 0xc0000004), (1, 0xc0000003), (3, 0xc0000005), (7, 0xc0000007), (4, 0xc0000006), (0xc, 0xc000000c), (0xd, 0xc000000d), (0xe, 0xc000000e), (0x15, 0xc0000001), (9, 0xc000001e), (6, 0xc0000009)`. All class IDs are in the 0xC0000000..0xC0000FF range (engine-managed pattern from BCS-Y-0533). This is the zone-init batch that creates the core actor set (camera, player, npc base, etc.). Note: FUN_004d90c0's `param_1` is the dispatcher's `this` (ECX register), and the visible args are `param_2 = interface_index` and `param_3 = class_id` - this differs from the case-0xCA AddActor invocation in FUN_004DC690 which is `FUN_004d90c0(*(zone+0x10), packet)` - so the call shape is `FUN_004d90c0(interface, class_id_or_packet_with_id_in_it)`.
key_findings.implication: FUN_004d9110 confirms FUN_004d90c0 is dispatched for EVERY actor creation - both the static zone-load actors AND the dynamic packet-driven AddActor cases. The 11 hardcoded class IDs in FUN_004d9110 are the engine-managed class set; these are the IDs registered in FUN_00d35af0 (BCS-Y-0533's registry). Useful catalog entry: enumerate the engine-managed class id space.

key_findings.title: FUN_004daa10 calls slot 8 (offset 0x20) of looked-up actors with sync events
key_findings.detail: FUN_004daa10 is a sync-queue processor that calls FUN_004ddb50 (atomic-queue dequeue via InterlockedCompareExchange on zone+0x1793c) to pull a sync event, then either calls `zone->slot17924->vtable[6](-1, ..)` for type-2 events (probably a UI/HUD update), or for other types calls `actor = FUN_004d9910(*(event+0x10)); actor->vtable[8](uVar5, event+0x20, uVar2)` where slot 8 is the per-actor sync event handler.
key_findings.implication: This is the Pattern B question from the actor cluster dispatch model pass and the actor vtable9 bulk pass viewed from a different angle - the per-actor polymorphic dispatch IS used by the engine, but at slot 8 (offset 0x20), not slot 9 (offset 0x24). Worth a low switch remaining cases follow-up: dump slot 8 (offset 0x20) for the same 5 cataloged actor classes and see if THAT is the real polymorphic actor event handler that the actor vtable9 bulk pass was looking for but missed by checking slot 9 instead.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: ControlActor_CharaBase_FinalizeLifecycleHook_FUN_006fa7e0
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: vtable[5] (slot offset 0x14) of Control::CharaBase, Control::PlayerBase, Control::NpcBase. Lua-side lifecycle/finalize hook called by FUN_004d90c0 (BCS-Y-0531) after the dispatched constructor returns AND from other lifecycle contexts. Body: (1) FUN_00cc7510 stack-cookie helper; (2) FUN_0076f010(child_id) - skip-if-engine-managed Lua hash dereg; (3) FUN_00766b30(this, child_id) - STL-map find+erase on the actor's INTERNAL child map at this+0x8..+0xc (NOT zone+0x17804); (4) FUN_006f6900(this, child_id, &context) - dispatches Lua _onFinalize N-API; (5) if `*(this+0xd8) != 0` (a flag), FUN_006f9040(this, child_id, &context) - resource cleanup (frees *(this+0x20), zeros *(this+0x60)). Operates on the actor's own internal data, not the zone-side actor map.
proposed_bcs_y_entries.notes: This drill's entry. The original task hypothesis was that this slot 5 was the zone-actor-map insert hook; the decomp refutes that. This is a class-internal lifecycle/finalize hook.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: vtable[5] of Control::MyPlayer. Wraps the shared CharaBase slot 5 (FUN_006fa7e0 = BCS-Y-0535) with MyPlayer-specific prefatory cleanup: if `*(this+0x110) != 0`, tags `*(this+0x110)+0xc = 4` (state byte to 'cancelled' value), calls FUN_006f7cd0 which dispatches `_onCancelJobQuestCompleteFirst`/`Second`/`Third` Lua N-APIs (selected by a state at +0xc of the subobject), then _free's it. Then delegates to FUN_006fa7e0.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: CharaActor_DelegateSlot5_FUN_00620700
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: vtable[5] of Application::Scene::Actor::Chara::CharaActor (engine-side, NOT Lua-side Control:: hierarchy). DELEGATE pattern: if `param_1[2] != 0` (the wrapped subobject), forwards via `param_1[2]->vtable[5](param_2, param_3, param_4, param_5)` (invokes the wrapped object's slot 5). Otherwise formats an error string via __snprintf_s with format at &DAT_00fb8660 plus the result of `(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))()` (vtable[13] of self - probably class-name string getter), appends '\n', calls `(*PTR_FUN_012651b4)(buf, 3)` which is the engine's tagged debug-print sink. CharaActor is a wrapper; the real work is in the wrapped object's slot 5, NOT here. Confirms the actor vftable9 investigation pass's finding that the engine-side CharaActor is a wrapper class.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: ZoneActorMap_FreeSlotIdAlloc_FUN_004d9ca0
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: Allocates the lowest unused actor id in [param_2..param_3) by probing the zone actor map at zone+0x17804..+0x17808. Iterates `uVar3 = param_2; uVar3 < param_3`, calling FUN_0071d420(&local_10, &uVar3) (STL map lower_bound) and checking if the slot is occupied (`*(local_c + 0x10) == 0` = free) - returns `uVar3` for the first hit. Returns 0xC0000000 if no free slot found. Sole caller: FUN_006ac9f0 (Lua-side allocator wrapper).
proposed_bcs_y_entries.notes: This drill's entry. This is a READ-only helper that anchors the actor-id allocation half of the create-actor path. The companion INSERT primitive (which actually writes to zone+0x17804..+0x17808) was NOT identified in this drill but is the natural next-phase target.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: ZoneActorMap_DestroyEntry_FUN_004dac20
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: Destroys an actor entry from the zone actor map at zone+0x17804..+0x17808. Body: (1) `actor->vtable[11]()` (offset 0x2c - per-actor destroy method); (2) if zone+0xb4 is non-null and not actor itself, call its vtable[21] (offset 0x54) with `actor->vtable[11]()` result (some UI update); (3) FUN_00563920(actor) if zone+0x4c0 differs from null and from actor (probably 'remove from active list'); (4) FUN_005374d0(actor[0x22]) - per-id de-init; (5) FUN_0071d420 lower_bound on zone+0x17804 with actor[0x22] = id; (6) if zone+0x17820 byte is 0 (safe-to-erase flag), call FUN_004de280(iter) for full STL map erase + if id has engine-managed pattern (top byte 0xC0..0xDF, subtype < 3) call FUN_00d35b30(id & 0xffffff) to deregister from FUN_00d35af0's engine-class registry; (7) if zone+0x17820 != 0 (deferred-remove mode), zero the slot's *(iter+0x10)=0 and call FUN_00813050(iter+0xc) for a node-only free; (8) if zone+0x17834 == actor, clear `actor->parent_zone[0x1f][0x17834]` (probably 'currently-controlled' actor); (9) if zone+0x17838 == actor, call FUN_004d9980(0xc0000000) (BCS-Y-0501 active-actor switcher). Callers: FUN_004db6a0, FUN_0068dd10.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: StlMap_EraseNode_FUN_004de280
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: MSVC STL `_Tree::_Erase_node` for the engine's actor maps. 693 bytes; full red-black-tree rebalance. Verifies the iterator is not the sentinel (`*(iter+0x15) != 0` would throw 'invalid map/set<T> iterator' via __CxxThrowException with type info at DAT_011aa734). Updates parent/left/right pointers (`*piVar5` and `piVar5[2]`), rebalances colors via FUN_0096fd70 (_Lmost), FUN_0081e910 (_Rmost), FUN_006ceef0 (_Lrotate), FUN_00b9f240 (_Rrotate). Final: FUN_0044d350(node, 0x18, 0x20) frees the 24-byte node (size 0x18, alignment 0x20). Decrements `*(this+8)` (the _Mysize field). Note: at VA 0x004DE4D0 there's a DUPLICATE/Aliased entry pointing to the same function body (Ghidra labels it FUN_004de280 - same name, same body).

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: StlMap_RangeErase_FUN_004de540
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: MSVC STL range-erase: calls FUN_004de280 (BCS-Y-0540) in a loop for each node in the range. Special-case for full-clear: if both [first, last) span the whole tree, does FUN_004ddad0 on the header node, resets all 4 sentinel pointers in one shot. Callers: FUN_004de900 (full-clear from unwinds), FUN_004dea00 (clear from FUN_004da680), FUN_004dea70 (full-clear from FUN_004deb50 and FUN_004dbaf0 and 2 unwinds).

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: ZoneActor_BatchCreateStaticActors_FUN_004d9110
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: Zone-load batch actor creator. Calls FUN_004d90c0 (BCS-Y-0531) with 11 hardcoded (interface_index, class_id) pairs: (2,0xc0000004), (1,0xc0000003), (3,0xc0000005), (7,0xc0000007), (4,0xc0000006), (0xc,0xc000000c), (0xd,0xc000000d), (0xe,0xc000000e), (0x15,0xc0000001), (9,0xc000001e), (6,0xc0000009). Conditional branches gate creation by `param_2 != 0` (re-init flag) and by FUN_00443e40(2,8,0) (game-mode/zone-type query). For mode in {2,3,4,5,6,7,8}, also creates index 6 with class 0xc0000009 and calls FUN_004d7ea0 then FUN_00565aa0. All 11 class_ids are in the 0xC0000000..0xC000001E range - the engine-managed class id space documented in BCS-Y-0533. Sole caller: FUN_004d9260 (a zone-load entrypoint).
proposed_bcs_y_entries.notes: First direct evidence of the engine-managed class id space's actual contents: 11 of the ~30 possible IDs in 0xC000000X are enumerated here as static zone actors.

proposed_bcs_y_entries.name: ZoneActor_SyncEventQueueProcessor_FUN_004daa10
proposed_bcs_y_entries.summary: Drains the zone's sync event queue (at zone+0x17938..+0x1793c, atomically synchronized via Interlocked* family) and dispatches each event polymorphically. Per event: if event_type (event+0x14) == 2, calls `zone->slot17924->vtable[6](-1, scaled_value)` (UI/HUD update path with sVar1 = event+0x20 scaled into 0..5 + percentage); for other types, calls `actor = FUN_004d9910(event+0x10); actor->vtable[8](event_subtype-3, event+0x20, event+0x18)` - SLOT 8 (offset 0x20) of the per-actor vtable. After dispatch, atomically clears the queue slot (InterlockedExchange to 0) and decrements the count (InterlockedDecrement on zone+0x17938). After the queue drains, calls `zone->slot17920->vtable[5](->slot+0x14)` (offset 0x14 - probably a 'sync complete' notification). Sole caller: FUN_004b3c50.

open_questions.q: Where is the actual zone+0x17804 actor map INSERT site? What function writes a new (actor_id, actor_ptr) pair into this map?
open_questions.approach_a: Drill FUN_004dac20 (BCS-Y-0539 candidate) and its callers FUN_004db6a0 + FUN_0068dd10. By symmetry the insert should be a sibling at similar VA. The FUN_004db6a0 function may pair with FUN_004db5b0 (caller of FUN_004daf00) as 'insert before clear' or 'transactional swap'.
open_questions.approach_b: Drill FUN_006ac9f0 - sole caller of FUN_004d9ca0 (BCS-Y-0538). It allocates a free id; whatever it does NEXT with that id is the insert.
open_questions.approach_c: Write a Ghidra script that scans .text for `MOV [reg+0x17808], reg` (size increment) instructions and lists containing functions. The insert MUST do this. Most direct path.
open_questions.approach_d: Take FUN_00537620 (BCS-Y-0530)'s method-table dispatch: enumerate the method table at zone+0x10's `+4..+8` range to find the 'create' method indices. The constructor method (likely index 5 - 'create actor of class X') runs the actual `new ClassX()` allocation; whether THAT writes the result to zone+0x17804 is the missing piece. Requires finding what writes to zone+0x10.

open_questions.q: What is the actor TYPE actually stored in the zone+0x17804 map at +0x10 of each node?
